text:
Thirteen points in 18 games looks like a second-line center doing his job. The picture underneath is harsher for Chandler Stephenson. At five-on-five, Seattle has taken only 37% of the shot attempts and 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 10 points worse than the Kraken manage without him. Evolving-Hockey flagged the same problem last season: opponents gained 0.39 expected goals per 60 with him out there, bottom 1% of forwards, though he also played beside some of the weakest teammates in the league.

Six of his points have come on the power play, where the passing still works. He has 14 shots all season, which tells you who he is now: a setup man who rarely pulls the trigger himself.

Some of this is bad luck. Seattle has scored about four fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that tends to swing back. The shot share is the bigger worry. For a two-time Stanley Cup winner at 32, the thing to watch is whether his 17:22 a night starts drifting toward younger centers.
